analysis.title: Higher inflation need not derail US assets (UBS House View - Daily Asia)
key_insights: UBS CIO says September US inflation came in above expectations and raised odds of further Fed hikes, but it does not expect the higher rate and yield outlook to undermine its positive view on US assets.

Headline inflation rose 0.6% m/m in September from 0.4% in August, driven largely by a 9.1% rise in gasoline prices. Core rose 0.3% m/m versus 0.2% consensus, for a second consecutive month, and the annual core rate rose to 2.6% from 2.4%.
Price increases extended beyond energy to shelter, airfares, vehicles, apparel and technology-related goods. UBS says this breadth makes the strength hard for the Fed to dismiss.

UBS now expects Fed hikes in December and March, following the September hike, then a hold until late 2027. It raised its end-December 10-year Treasury yield forecast to 4.9% from 4.6%, which is below the current 5.24%.

Markets price roughly 3.5 further hikes after September, versus two additional hikes in UBS's baseline. The gap leaves room for yields to fall if the Fed waits in October and data show inflation stabilizing.

Market odds of an October hike rose to about 47% from about 20% before the CPI release. The 2-year Treasury yield rose 11 bps to 4.90%. NY Fed President Williams said there is 'no need for urgency', but two straight hot core prints make October a closer call.

UBS argues economic strength supports equities: US GDP growth near 2.5% annualized in 1H and likely near 3% in Q3. September payrolls slowed to 29,000, but the 3-month average of 51,000 is in line with the pace needed to keep unemployment stable. Initial claims hit a 10-week low and ISM manufacturing was 54.5 in September.

UBS forecasts S&P 500 EPS growth of 28% for the September quarter, driven by AI demand, cyclical improvement and resilient consumer spending. AI-related spending is estimated to rise 84% this year to USD 900bn, with semiconductor profits about half of Q3 S&P 500 earnings growth.

The ISM manufacturing new-orders component has been in expansion for nine consecutive months. Across 16 Fed hiking cycles since 1954, the S&P 500 gained an average of 10.8% in the year after the first hike.

UBS stays positioned for further equity gains with broad diversification across sectors and regions, and sees value in quality fixed income because higher starting yields give income and a 10-year decline to 4.9% would give capital gains.

Germany plans to press the EU to consider safeguards on Chinese chemicals, mechanical engineering products and potentially pharmaceuticals, after a record USD 34.8bn Chinese goods surplus with the EU in September (about 21% higher y/y; exports above USD 60bn for the first time). The EU has agreed to cap Chinese hybrid-vehicle imports at 350,000 units a year, potentially from 1 December.

UBS says broader EU trade defenses could cause near-term volatility and dispersion but are not a reason to cut risk assets. It favors companies with strong balance sheets, pricing power and diversified supply chains, and capital preservation strategies and broad commodities as diversifiers.

The MAS surprised by holding Singapore dollar policy unchanged, pausing a tightening cycle that included April and July increases. It kept the slope, width and center of the band, and narrowed its 2026 core inflation forecast to 1.5-2.0% while keeping 1.5-2.5% for 2027. USDSGD was just above 1.28, and UBS still expects a gradual decline to 1.25 over 12 months.

ASML raised the low end of its 2026 revenue forecast for a third straight quarter and reported stronger-than-expected September-quarter earnings. It said it cannot fully meet demand in 2027 and 2028, customers have asked about 2029 and 2030 orders, and it is exploring more 2028 capacity beyond the 30% expansion announced in July.

UBS says ASML's results came after sharp recent declines in global semiconductor shares on AI demand, financing, rising rates and competition worries. UBS expects continued AI supply chain investment and favors diversified AI exposure across high-quality semiconductor and hardware names, mega-cap platforms and defensive technology.

sector_views.rationale: ASML's results point to robust AI compute and infrastructure demand. UBS favors high-quality semiconductor and hardware beneficiaries, mega-cap platforms and defensive technology, while warning of volatility from slowing capex growth, financing needs and monetization concerns.
ISM manufacturing new orders have been in expansion for nine consecutive months, supporting industrial profits. UBS favors a combination of cyclical and secular equity exposure.
Higher starting yields provide income, and UBS's forecast of a 10-year yield at 4.9% by end-December leaves room for capital gains.

earnings_insights: UBS forecasts S&P 500 EPS growth of 28% for the September quarter (UBS forecast, not yet reported), supported by AI demand, cyclical improvement and resilient consumer spending.
Semiconductor profits are expected to account for about half of S&P 500 earnings growth in the third quarter (UBS expectation).

ASML reported stronger-than-expected September-quarter earnings (reported Wednesday 14 October; no EPS figure given in this note) and raised the low end of its 2026 revenue forecast for a third consecutive quarter.

risk_factors: Further hot inflation prints could push the Fed to hike in October and beyond the path UBS expects.
Slowing AI capex growth, financing requirements, monetization concerns and execution risks may cause bouts of volatility in the AI trade.
Broader EU trade defenses against China could raise uncertainty for internationally integrated businesses and increase the risk of Chinese retaliation.
The 10-year Treasury yield at 5.24% is above UBS's end-December forecast of 4.9%.
vol_and_positioning: Markets raised the probability of an October Fed hike to about 47% from about 20% before the CPI release.
Markets price roughly 3.5 further Fed hikes beyond September, versus UBS's baseline of two more.
Global semiconductor shares fell sharply in recent days on AI demand, financing, rising rates and competition concerns before ASML's results.
UBS suggests capital preservation strategies to retain equity exposure while limiting losses in a market setback.
geopolitical: Germany plans to press the EU to consider safeguards on Chinese chemicals, mechanical engineering products and potentially pharmaceuticals, per a Bloomberg report.
The EU has agreed to cap Chinese hybrid-vehicle imports at 350,000 units annually, potentially from 1 December, with a risk of Chinese retaliation from wider restrictions.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS expects only two more hikes (December, March), then a hold until late 2027. Strong growth, earnings and a 16-cycle average 10.8% gain in the year after the first hike let equities absorb moderately higher rates.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets price about 3.5 further hikes, and two straight above-consensus core prints with broad price pressure make an October hike a closer call, with the 10-year at 5.24%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further hot inflation data pushing the Fed to hike in October, or a path beyond UBS's December and March hikes.

tension_points.bull_case: ASML raised its 2026 revenue outlook for a third quarter, expects to be unable to meet 2027-2028 demand, and reports customer interest in 2029-2030 orders.
tension_points.bear_case: Slowing capex growth, financing requirements, monetization concerns and execution risks may cause volatility, and global semiconductor shares fell sharply in recent days.

theme_stances.key_argument: Economic strength allowing the Fed to raise rates also supports equities, so they can absorb moderately higher rates.
theme_stances.evidence: Markets are pricing a more aggressive rate path than we expect.

theme_stances.key_argument: ASML's earnings point to robust underlying demand for AI compute and infrastructure, supporting continued investment across the AI supply chain.
theme_stances.evidence: ASML's earnings point to robust underlying demand for AI compute and infrastructure.

theme_stances.key_argument: Broader EU trade defenses could create near-term volatility and dispersion but are not a reason to retreat from risk assets.
theme_stances.evidence: trade tensions alone are not a reason to retreat from risk assets
